verdict.rationale: Codegen is an agent platform, so MCP-client evidence would not count here: integrating third-party MCP servers (codegen-docs-26) and provisioning them across the org (codegen-docs-7) are client-side. However, the CLI wraps local Claude Code and "provides access to your Codegen integrations via MCP injection" (codegen-docs-30). That suggests Codegen exposes its own capabilities over MCP to an external agent, though only through its CLI wrapper and in a single thin mention. missing for 10: a documented standalone official MCP server or hosted MCP endpoint, a list of the tools it exposes (e.g., creating or managing agent runs), setup docs for connecting arbitrary MCP clients, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
